main_text.p: cium absoluat. Est autem iustum precium, quod saltem veri precij partem dimidiam adæquat. verum autē, quanti communi hominum æsti-matione res est. quare ut supleat emptor, unum addere debebit. His positis, quæro vicissim de emptore hoc modo: Titius equum decem aureorum, emit sexdecim. Re cognita, queritur, se ultra dimidium rei precium fraudatum: &, ut venditio rescinda-tur, petit. nam venditoris eadem, quæ emptoris, ratio esse debet. At vēditor tum erat deceptus, cum rei precium erat amplius dimidio diminutum:

page.notes: The left margin holds a printed ornamental mark (a hand-like sign, not legible text); it is not transcribed as a note. The running head is a black-letter style title that I cannot read letter by letter. Doubtful: "vēditor" (the macron stands for a missing n; read as "uēditor" in print). "absoluat" begins the page as a fragment; the first word is read as "cium absoluat" with the first letters cut by the binding edge, so "cium" is a fragment per the rule, and the start "absoluat" is printed as "abfoluat". Printed spelling "abfoluat" is kept as an s-form, and "precium" is kept as printed. The word "ut fup / pleat" is a line break without a hyphen and is written whole as "supleat".
